findings.title: Early interpolation bypasses the $__range splitting guard
findings.body: `runSplitQuery` now interpolates each query via `applyTemplateVariables` before passing it to `querySupportsSplitting`. That check intentionally calls `isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr)` to avoid splitting queries that use `$__range`, because each split chunk would otherwise evaluate the range variable against the wrong range. After interpolation, `$__range` is replaced by a literal duration, so `isQueryWithRangeVariable` no longer matches and these queries are split. Each chunk then uses the full-range duration instead of the chunk range, producing overlapping/duplicated results for range-based aggregations. The range-variable check must inspect the original expression, or interpolation must happen after that classification.

findings.title: Shard path interpolates every target twice
findings.body: `runShardSplitQuery` now calls `applyTemplateVariables` on each target, then passes the already-interpolated targets into `runSplitQuery`, which also calls `applyTemplateVariables` on its targets. The updated shard test asserts five interpolation calls, confirming this double application. This is not safe to assume idempotent: `applyTemplateVariables` receives `request.filters`, so ad-hoc filters can be appended on both passes, and variable values that themselves contain `$...` patterns can be expanded a second time, changing the LogQL sent to Loki. Interpolation should occur once at the entry point, or `runSplitQuery` needs an option to skip interpolation when its caller has already done it.
